## `install`#

Installs an environment based on the manifest file. If there is no `pixi.lock` file or it is not up-to-date with the manifest file, it will (re-)generate the lock file.

`pixi install` only installs one environment at a time, if you have multiple environments you can select the right one with the `--environment` flag. If you don't provide an environment, the `default` environment will be installed.

Running `pixi install` is not required before running other commands. As all commands interacting with the environment will first run the `install` command if the environment is not ready, to make sure you always run in a correct state. E.g. `pixi run`, `pixi shell`, `pixi shell-hook`, `pixi add`, `pixi remove` to name a few.

##### Options#

  * `--manifest-path <MANIFEST_PATH>`: the path to manifest file, by default it searches for one in the parent directories.
  * `--frozen`: install the environment as defined in the lock file, doesn't update `pixi.lock` if it isn't up-to-date with manifest file. It can also be controlled by the `PIXI_FROZEN` environment variable (example: `PIXI_FROZEN=true`).
  * `--locked`: only install if the `pixi.lock` is up-to-date with the manifest file^{1}. It can also be controlled by the `PIXI_LOCKED` environment variable (example: `PIXI_LOCKED=true`). Conflicts with `--frozen`.
  * `--environment <ENVIRONMENT> (-e)`: The environment to install, if none are provided the default environment will be used.
    
    `pixi install
    pixi install --manifest-path ~/myproject/pixi.toml
    pixi install --frozen
    pixi install --locked
    pixi install --environment lint
    pixi install -e lint
    `

To reinitialize the lock file in your project, you can remove the existing `pixi.lock` file and run `pixi install`. This process will regenerate the lock file based on the dependencies defined in your manifest file:
    
    `rm pixi.lock && pixi install
    `

This action ensures that your project's dependencies are reset and updated according to the current specifications in manifest file.

In a future version of `pixi`, we will introduce the `pixi update` command, see #73. This command will allow you to update the lock file directly, without manually deleting the `pixi.lock` file, making the dependency management process even smoother.

## `update`#

The `update` command checks if there are newer versions of the dependencies and updates the `pixi.lock` file and environments accordingly. It will only update the lock file if the dependencies in the manifest file are still compatible with the new versions.

##### Arguments#

  1. `[PACKAGES]...` The packages to update, space separated. If no packages are provided, all packages will be updated.

##### Options#

  * `--manifest-path <MANIFEST_PATH>`: the path to manifest file, by default it searches for one in the parent directories.
  * `--environment <ENVIRONMENT> (-e)`: The environment to install, if none are provided all the environments are updated.
  * `--platform <PLATFORM> (-p)`: The platform for which the dependencies should be updated.
  * `--dry-run (-n)`: Only show the changes that would be made, without actually updating the lock file or environment.
  * `--no-install`: Don't install the (solve) environment needed for solving pypi-dependencies.
    
    `pixi update numpy
    pixi update numpy pandas
    pixi update --manifest-path ~/myproject/pixi.toml numpy
    pixi update --environment lint python
    pixi update -e lint -e schema -e docs pre-commit
    pixi update --platform osx-arm64 mlx
    pixi update -p linux-64 -p osx-64 numpy
    pixi update --dry-run
    pixi update --no-install boto3
    `

Pixi is a single executable and can be run without any external dependencies. That means you can manually download the suitable archive for your architecture and operating system from our GitHub releases, unpack it and then use it as is. If you want `pixi` itself or the executables installed via `pixi global` to be available in your `PATH`, you have to add them manually. The executables are located in PIXI_HOME/bin.

### Install From Source#

pixi is 100% written in Rust, and therefore it can be installed, built and tested with cargo. To start using Pixi from a source build run:
    
    `cargo install --locked --git https://github.com/prefix-dev/pixi.git pixi
    `

We don't publish to `crates.io` anymore, so you need to install it from the repository. The reason for this is that we depend on some unpublished crates which disallows us to publish to `crates.io`.

or when you want to make changes use:
    
    `cargo build
    cargo test
    `

If you have any issues building because of the dependency on `rattler` checkout its compile steps.

L366: 
L367: To install `pixi` you can run the following command in your terminal:
L368: 
L369: [Input][Input]
L370: 
L371: Linux & macOS Windows
L372: 
L373:     `curl -fsSL https://pixi.sh/install.sh | sh
L374:     `
L375: 
L376: If your system doesn't have `curl`, you can use `wget`:
L377: 
L378:     `wget -qO- https://pixi.sh/install.sh | sh
L379:     `
L380: 
L381: What does this do?
L382: The above invocation will automatically download the latest version of `pixi`, extract it, and move the `pixi` binary to `~/.pixi/bin`. The script will also extend the `PATH` environment variable in the startup script of your shell to include `~/.pixi/bin`. This allows you to invoke `pixi` from anywhere.
L383: 
L384: cite223†Download installer†github.com L385: 
L386: Or run:
L387: 
L388:     `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -c "irm -useb https://pixi.sh/install.ps1 | iex"
L389:     `
L390: 
L391: What does this do?
L392: The above invocation will automatically download the latest version of `pixi`, extract it, and move the `pixi` binary to `%UserProfile%\.pixi\bin`. The command will also add `%UserProfile%\.pixi\bin` to your `PATH` environment variable, allowing you to invoke `pixi` from anywhere.
L393: 
L394: Now restart your terminal or shell to make the installation take effect.
L395: 
L396: Don't trust our link? Check the script!
L397: You can check the installation `sh` script: cite224†download†pixi.sh and the `ps1`: cite225†download†pixi.sh . The scripts are open source and available on cite226†GitHub†github.com .
L398: 
L399: Telemetry
L400: 
L401: After a successful install the script sends a single anonymous ping so we can count installations. Prefix `PIXI_NO_TELEMETRY=1` (or `DO_NOT_TRACK=1`) to the command above to opt out, e.g. `curl -fsSL https://pixi.sh/install.sh | PIXI_NO_TELEMETRY=1 bash`. See cite217†Telemetry for what is sent.
L402: Don't forget to add autocompletion!
L403: 
L404: After installing Pixi, you can enable autocompletion for your shell. See the cite12†Autocompletion section below for instructions.
L405: ## Updatecite0†# L406: 
L407: Updating is as simple as installing, rerunning the installation script gets you the latest version.
L408: 
L409:     `pixi self-update
L410:     `
L411: 
L412: Or get a specific Pixi version using:
L413: 
L414:     `pixi self-update --version x.y.z
L415:     `
L416: 
L417: Note
L418: 
L419: If you've used a package manager like `brew`, `mamba`, `conda`, `paru` etc. to install `pixi` you must use the built-in update mechanism. e.g. `brew upgrade pixi`.
L420: ## Alternative Installation Methodscite4†# L421: 
L422: Although we recommend installing Pixi through the above method we also provide additional installation methods.
L423: 
L424: ### Homebrewcite5†# L425: 
L426: Pixi is available via homebrew. To install Pixi via homebrew simply run:
L427: 
L428:     `brew install pixi
L429:     `
L430: 
L431: ### Windows Installercite6†# L432: 
L433: We provide an `msi` installer on cite227†our GitHub releases page†github.com . The installer will download Pixi and add it to the `PATH`.
L434: 
L435: ### Wingetcite7†# L436: 
L437:     `winget install prefix-dev.pixi
L438:     `
L439: ### Scoopcite8†# L440: 
L441:     `scoop install main/pixi
L442:     `
L443: ### Download From GitHub Releasescite9†# L444: 
L445: Pixi is a single executable and can be run without any external dependencies. That means you can manually download the suitable archive for your architecture and operating system from our cite228†GitHub releases†github.com , unpack it and then use it as is. If you want `pixi` itself or the executables installed via `pixi global` to be available in your `PATH`, you have to add them manually. The executables are located in cite216†PIXI_HOME /bin.
L446: ### Install From Sourcecite10†# L447: 
L448: pixi is 100% written in Rust, and therefore it can be installed, built and tested with cargo. To start using Pixi from a source build run:
L449: 
L450:     `cargo install --locked --git https://github.com/prefix-dev/pixi.git pixi
L451:     `
L452: 
L453: We don't publish to `crates.io` anymore, so you need to install it from the repository. The reason for this is that we depend on some unpublished crates which disallows us to publish to `crates.io`.
L454: or when you want to make changes use:
L455: 
L456:     `cargo build
L457:     cargo test
L458:     `
L459: 
L460: If you have any issues building because of the dependency on `rattler` check out its cite229†compile steps†github.com .
L461: ## Installer Script Optionscite11†# L462: 
L463: [Input][Input]
L464: 
L465: Linux & macOS Windows
L466: 
L467: The installation script has several options that can be manipulated through environment variables.
L468: Variable  | Description  | Default Value
L469: --- | --- | ---
L470: `PIXI_VERSION`  | The version of Pixi getting installed, can be used to up- or down-grade.  | `latest`
L471: `PIXI_HOME`  | The location of the pixi home folder containing global environments and configs.  | `$HOME/.pixi`
L472: `PIXI_BIN_DIR`  | The location where the standalone pixi binary should be installed.  | `$PIXI_HOME/bin`
L473: `PIXI_ARCH`  | The architecture the Pixi version was built for.  | `uname -m`
L474: `PIXI_NO_PATH_UPDATE`  | If set the `$PATH` will not be updated to add `pixi` to it.  |
L475: `PIXI_DOWNLOAD_URL`  | Overrides the download URL for the Pixi binary (useful for mirrors or custom builds).  | GitHub releases, e.g. cite230†linux-64†github.com L476: `NETRC`  | Path to a custom `.netrc` file for authentication with private repositories.  |
L477: `TMP_DIR`  | The temporary directory the script uses to download to and unpack the binary from.  | `/tmp`
L478: `PIXI_NO_TELEMETRY`  | If set, the script will not send the anonymous installation ping (cite217†Telemetry ).  |
L479: `DO_NOT_TRACK`  | Same as `PIXI_NO_TELEMETRY`; honors the common `DO_NOT_TRACK` convention.  |
L480: For example, on Apple Silicon, you can force the installation of the x86 version:
L481: 
L482:     `curl -fsSL https://pixi.sh/install.sh | PIXI_ARCH=x86_64 bash
L483:     `
L484: 
L485: Or set the version
L486: 
L487:     `curl -fsSL https://pixi.sh/install.sh | PIXI_VERSION=v0.18.0 bash
L488:     `
L489: 
L490: To make a "drop-in" installation of pixi directly in the user `$PATH`:
L491: 
L492:     `curl -fsSL https://pixi.sh/install.sh | PIXI_BIN_DIR=/usr/local/bin PIXI_NO_PATH_UPDATE=1 bash
L493:     `
L494: #### Using `.netrc` for Authenticationcite231†# L495: 
L496: If you need to download Pixi from a private repository that requires authentication, you can use a `.netrc` file instead of hardcoding credentials in the `PIXI_DOWNLOAD_URL`.
L497: The install script automatically uses `.netrc` for authentication with `curl` and `wget`. By default, it looks for `~/.netrc`. You can specify a custom location using the `NETRC` environment variable:
L498: 
L499:     `# Use the default ~/.netrc file
L500:     curl -fsSL https://pixi.sh/install.sh | PIXI_DOWNLOAD_URL=https://private.example.com/pixi-latest.tar.gz bash
L501:     `
L502: 
L503:     `# Use a custom .netrc file
L504:     curl -fsSL https://pixi.sh/install.sh | NETRC=/path/to/custom/.netrc PIXI_DOWNLOAD_URL=https://private.example.com/pixi-latest.tar.gz bash
L505:     `
L506: Your `.netrc` file should contain credentials in the following format:
L507: 
L508:     `machine private.example.com
L509:     login your-username
L510:     password your-token-or-password
L511:     `
L512: 
L513: Security Recommendation
L514: 
L515: Using `.netrc` is more secure than embedding credentials directly in the `PIXI_DOWNLOAD_URL` (e.g., `REDACTED`), as it keeps credentials separate from the URL and prevents them from appearing in logs or process listings.
L516: 
L517: Security Note
L518: The install script automatically masks any credentials embedded in the download URL when displaying messages, replacing them with `***:***@` to prevent credentials from appearing in logs or console output.

L529: For example, set the version:

def entry_point(obj: Object) -> Probe:
    """must/007 (instructions for install and usage) and must/008 (a starting point)."""
    readmes = [p for p in obj.tracked() if p.lower() in {"readme.md", "readme.rst", "readme", "readme.txt"}]
    makefiles = [p for p in obj.tracked() if p in {"Makefile", "makefile", "GNUmakefile"}]
    items = ["stamped-checklist:must/007", "stamped-checklist:must/008"]
    tracked = set(obj.tracked())
    make_text = "\n".join(obj.read(p) for p in makefiles)
    readme_text = "\n".join(obj.read(p) for p in readmes)
    text = readme_text + "\n" + make_text

    targets = [t for t in re.findall(r"^([a-zA-Z0-9_.%/-]+):\s*(?:[^=]|$)", make_text, re.M) if not t.startswith(".")]
    workflow = sorted(p for p in tracked if p.rsplit("/", 1)[-1] in {"Snakefile", "main.nf", "dvc.yaml"}
                      or p.endswith(".smk"))
    named = sorted(p for p in tracked if p.endswith(RUNNABLE_SUFFIXES)
                   and (p in text or p.rsplit("/", 1)[-1] in text))
    # A heading is the common shape, not the only one: `1. Install FSL`,
    # `**Usage**` and a numbered list of steps are all instructions, and a real
    # README (ReproNim/simple_workflow) lost must/007 for using the second
    # form. The question the item asks is whether instructions exist, not
    # whether they are under a Markdown heading.
    # And a heading need not *begin* with the word: `## Entry point and
    # reproduce` over a block of commands, with `## Requirements` above it, is
    # install and usage however it is titled. A blind run wrote exactly that
    # pair and still lost must/007, which is the probe grading the prose style
    # rather than the question the item asks.
    has_section = bool(
        re.search(rf"(?im)^(?:#+|\s*\d+[.)]|\s*[-*]|\*\*|__)?\s*\**\b(?:{INSTRUCTION_WORDS})",
                  readme_text)
        or re.search(rf"(?im)^#+\s.*\b(?:{INSTRUCTION_WORDS})", readme_text)
    )
    # Commands the instructions tell a reader to run, checked against what the
    # tracked workflow actually defines. The probe used to hold both lists and
    # never compare them.
    documented_targets = {m for m in re.findall(r"(?<![\w-])make\s+(?:-[\w-]+\s+)*([a-zA-Z][\w.%/-]*)", readme_text)}
    documented_targets -= {"-n", "all"} if "all" not in targets else {"-n"}
    missing_targets = sorted(t for t in documented_targets if t not in set(targets)) if makefiles else []

    evidence = [Evidence(p, "instructions") for p in readmes + makefiles]
    evidence += [Evidence(p, "entry point named in the instructions and present") for p in named[:5]]
    if targets:
        evidence.append(Evidence(makefiles[0], f"make targets: {', '.join(sorted(set(targets))[:6])}"))
    if workflow:
        evidence.append(Evidence(workflow[0], "workflow definition"))

    # must/007: are there instructions for installation and usage?
    if missing_targets:
        s7 = "partial"
        r7 = clip(f"{readmes[0] if readmes else 'The instructions'} tells the reader to run "
                  f"`make {missing_targets[0]}`, which {makefiles[0]} does not define "
                  f"(targets: {', '.join(sorted(set(targets))[:5])}).")
    elif readmes and has_section:
        s7 = "met"
        r7 = clip(f"{readmes[0]} has an install/usage/reproduce section.")
    elif readmes and (targets or workflow):
        s7 = "partial"
        r7 = clip(f"{readmes[0]} has no install or usage section; usage is only implied by "
                  f"{makefiles[0] if targets else workflow[0]}.")
    elif targets:
        s7 = "partial"
        r7 = clip(f"No README; {makefiles[0]} carries the usage implicitly in its targets.")
    else:
        s7 = "unmet"
        r7 = "Neither a README with install/usage instructions nor a Makefile."

    # must/008: is there a clear starting point, and does it exist?
    starting = named[:1] or ([f"make {targets[0]}"] if targets else workflow[:1])
    if starting:
        s8 = "met"
        r8 = clip(f"Starting point present: {starting[0]}.")
    else:
        s8 = "unmet"
        r8 = clip("No script, make target or workflow definition that a reader could start from"
                  + (f" is named in {readmes[0]}." if readmes else "."))

    if missing_targets:
        evidence.insert(0, Evidence(f"{readmes[0] if readmes else makefiles[0]}",
                                    f"documents `make {missing_targets[0]}`; no such target"))
    worst = min((s7, s8), key=lambda s: {"unmet": 0, "partial": 1, "met": 2}[s])
    return Probe(
        "entry-point", worst, items, clip(f"must/007 {s7}: {r7} must/008 {s8}: {r8}"), evidence,
        {"readmes": readmes, "makefiles": makefiles, "named": named, "targets": sorted(set(targets)),
         "workflow": workflow, "has_section": has_section, "documented_targets": sorted(documented_targets),
         "missing_targets": missing_targets},
        item_status={items[0]: s7, items[1]: s8},
        item_reason={items[0]: r7, items[1]: r8},
    )

        or re.search(rf"(?im)^#+\s.*\b(?:{INSTRUCTION_WORDS})", readme_text)
    )
    # Commands the instructions tell a reader to run, checked against what the
    # tracked workflow actually defines. The probe used to hold both lists and
    # never compare them.
    documented_targets = {m for m in re.findall(r"(?<![\w-])make\s+(?:-[\w-]+\s+)*([a-zA-Z][\w.%/-]*)", readme_text)}
    documented_targets -= {"-n", "all"} if "all" not in targets else {"-n"}
    missing_targets = sorted(t for t in documented_targets if t not in set(targets)) if makefiles else []

    evidence = [Evidence(p, "instructions") for p in readmes + makefiles]
    evidence += [Evidence(p, "entry point named in the instructions and present") for p in named[:5]]
    if targets:
        evidence.append(Evidence(makefiles[0], f"make targets: {', '.join(sorted(set(targets))[:6])}"))
    if workflow:
        evidence.append(Evidence(workflow[0], "workflow definition"))

    # must/007: are there instructions for installation and usage?
    if missing_targets:
        s7 = "partial"
        r7 = clip(f"{readmes[0] if readmes else 'The instructions'} tells the reader to run "
                  f"`make {missing_targets[0]}`, which {makefiles[0]} does not define "
                  f"(targets: {', '.join(sorted(set(targets))[:5])}).")
    elif readmes and has_section:
        s7 = "met"
        r7 = clip(f"{readmes[0]} has an install/usage/reproduce section.")
    elif readmes and (targets or workflow):
        s7 = "partial"
        r7 = clip(f"{readmes[0]} has no install or usage section; usage is only implied by "
                  f"{makefiles[0] if targets else workflow[0]}.")
    elif targets:
        s7 = "partial"
        r7 = clip(f"No README; {makefiles[0]} carries the usage implicitly in its targets.")
    else:
        s7 = "unmet"
        r7 = "Neither a README with install/usage instructions nor a Makefile."

    # must/008: is there a clear starting point, and does it exist?
    starting = named[:1] or ([f"make {targets[0]}"] if targets else workflow[:1])
    if starting:
        s8 = "met"
        r8 = clip(f"Starting point present: {starting[0]}.")
    else:
        s8 = "unmet"
        r8 = clip("No script, make target or workflow definition that a reader could start from"
                  + (f" is named in {readmes[0]}." if readmes else "."))

    if missing_targets:
        evidence.insert(0, Evidence(f"{readmes[0] if readmes else makefiles[0]}",
                                    f"documents `make {missing_targets[0]}`; no such target"))
    worst = min((s7, s8), key=lambda s: {"unmet": 0, "partial": 1, "met": 2}[s])
    return Probe(
        "entry-point", worst, items, clip(f"must/007 {s7}: {r7} must/008 {s8}: {r8}"), evidence,
        {"readmes": readmes, "makefiles": makefiles, "named": named, "targets": sorted(set(targets)),
         "workflow": workflow, "has_section": has_section, "documented_targets": sorted(documented_targets),
         "missing_targets": missing_targets},
        item_status={items[0]: s7, items[1]: s8},
        item_reason={items[0]: r7, items[1]: r8},
    )

"""Link a completed duct analysis run to its exact inputs and environment."""
import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import platform
import sys
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

import nibabel
import nilearn
import numpy
import pandas
import scipy

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]


def sha256(path: Path) -> str:
    digest = hashlib.sha256()
    with path.open("rb") as stream:
        for block in iter(lambda: stream.read(1024 * 1024), b""):
            digest.update(block)
    return digest.hexdigest()


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--run-id", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--code-revision", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--log-prefix", required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    prefix = ROOT / args.log_prefix
    info_path = Path(str(prefix) + "info.json")
    info = json.loads(info_path.read_text())
    sources = json.loads((ROOT / "input/sources.json").read_text())
    outputs = sorted(p for p in (ROOT / "results").iterdir()
                     if p.is_file() and p.name != "report.md")
    manifest = {
        "run_id": args.run_id,
        "completed_at_utc": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
        "code_revision": args.code_revision,
        "working_tree_before_run": "clean" if not info.get("env", {}).get("GIT_DIRTY") else "dirty",
        "command": "pixi run duct ... pixi run analysis",
        "duct_info": str(info_path.relative_to(ROOT)),
        "duct_summary": info.get("execution_summary"),
        "environment": {
            "pixi_manifest_sha256": sha256(ROOT / "pixi.toml"),
            "pixi_lock_sha256": sha256(ROOT / "pixi.lock"),
            "python": sys.version.split()[0],
            "platform": platform.platform(),
            "packages": {"nibabel": nibabel.__version__, "nilearn": nilearn.__version__,
                         "numpy": numpy.__version__, "scipy": scipy.__version__,
                         "pandas": pandas.__version__},
        },
        "inputs": {
            "sources_manifest": {"path": "input/sources.json", "sha256": sha256(ROOT / "input/sources.json")},
            "participants_tsv": {"path": "input/participants.tsv", "sha256": sha256(ROOT / "input/participants.tsv")},
            "participant_maps": sources["files"],
        },
        "outputs": [{"path": str(path.relative_to(ROOT)), "bytes": path.stat().st_size,
                     "sha256": sha256(path)} for path in outputs],
    }
    destination = ROOT / "logs" / f"{args.run_id}-provenance.json"
    destination.write_text(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
    print(json.dumps({"run_provenance": str(destination.relative_to(ROOT)),
                      "outputs": len(outputs), "lock_sha256": manifest["environment"]["pixi_lock_sha256"]}, indent=2))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
